title: Prescriptive JSON Decoder Integration Tests for Structured Outputs
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Objective: Build an integration test suite that validates a prescriptive JSON decoding strategy across streaming responses, function/tool-calling payloads, and compatibility transformation layers. This ticket targets end-to-end tests (runtime + compatibility shim + SDK surface) that reduce regressions caused by tokenization boundaries, permissive decoders, and legacy-client assumptions. The goal is to establish repeatable cases that reflect production workloads (short chat turns, long-form streaming outputs, tool calls with nested argument objects) and ensure deterministic behavior for the Redwood API's structured-output modes.
steps: Create harness that can replay model streaming chunks as received from the runtime (including partial tokens and cut JSON tokens).

Test chunk-reassembly: stream a JSON object split across N chunks at random token boundaries; assert that the decoder reconstructs exactly one valid top-level JSON and that no trailing partial tokens leak into subsequent responses.

Constrained-decoding enforcement: feed inputs with schemas (required fields, enum constraints, typed fields) and try adversarial generations (extra keys, wrong types, nulls). Assert decoder rejects or sanitizes per enforcement mode (strict | permissive).

Function-calling integration: simulate models that emit function_call payloads with args that must match function schema. Validate both streaming and final payloads against the function signature (types, required params).

Compatibility shim tests: run legacy-client expectations (flat 'result' string) through the compatibility layer and ensure transform to new structured 'output' object is lossless for known mappings and logged for lossy mappings.

KV cache & tokenization: run tests with cold and warm KV cache to ensure the decoder behavior (esp. constrained decoding) is invariant to cache state and that prefix caching doesn't cause truncated JSON bodies.

Termination/early-stop tests: inject model terminations mid-JSON (stop tokens, early eos) and verify failure modes: decoder should raise a deterministic error code and emit tracing metadata for debugging.
Stress/fuzz pass: generate 10k small perturbations (whitespace changes, unexpected commas, order swaps) and confirm recovery thresholds and failure rates are within SLOs.
Integration with SDKs: run the same streamed-then-validate flow through the Python and Node SDK wrappers to catch surface-level parsing differences.
Add CI job that runs the deterministic subset (non-fuzz) on feature branches and nightly runs for fuzzing sampling.
Document all test cases and produce a short-runbook for triaging structured-output violations in production (include common fixes and PR templates).
acceptance_criteria: Test harness can replay streaming chunks at arbitrary token boundaries and reassemble into a single JSON document in >99.9% deterministic trials.
Constrained decoder enforces schemas in 'strict' mode (rejects unknown keys and wrong types) and provides normalized outputs in 'permissive' mode; both behaviors covered by unit+integration tests.
Function-calling payloads emitted during streaming are validated against function schemas; failures are surfaced to the SDK as structured errors with trace IDs.
Compatibility shim passes canonical mappings for legacy clients for all regression fixtures; any lossy mapping is recorded and surfaced to the console QA dashboard.
Nightly fuzz job runs without flakiness >98% for baseline scenarios and flags regressions with reproducible seeds.
Python and Node SDK wrappers parse the test-suite outputs identically (byte-for-byte equivalence for canonical fixtures).
CI job added and gated on feature branches touching structured-output, with green checks required before merge for changes touching the decoder or compatibility layer.
Runbook and triage checklist published to Confluence and linked from incident pages.
notes: 2025-02-10: Initial kickoff. Spike yesterday showed token-boundary bugs when streaming large arrays — repro harness in runtime-sim/stream-replay (prototype).

2025-02-12: Design sync with SDK owners (Samira & Josh). Decided to expose trace_id in parsing errors for easier correlation in Console. — decision: do not attempt to auto-correct type mismatches in strict mode; prefer explicit normalization in permissive path.

2025-02-14: Engineering review (Carlos): prototyped constrained decoder using PEG-based validator; trade-off is additional CPU in strict mode. Plan: strict mode enabled for Dedicated/Private by default; hosted will default permissive to save cycles and avoid user-visible latency increases.

2025-02-15: Blocker found — function-calling streaming frames emitted function args as plain text across two chunks, causing schema check to fail. Mitigation: add streaming assembly buffer with incremental JSON parsing and chunk sequence numbers.
2025-02-16: PR opened for stream-replay harness and basic constraints tests: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4123 — needs review from infra and SDK teams.

2025-02-17: PM feedback (Elena): include end-to-end customer scenario where user calls a downstream tool using the function-calling path and expects structured result mapping to a DB record. Adding that fixture to the acceptance list.
2025-02-18: Updated tests to include legacy-compat cases for older SDKs. Next steps: land CI job and add nightly fuzz sampling.
